title: Prospectuses for cash box and investment companies
subject: This guide addresses disclosure requirements for prospectuses of cash box and investment companies that have not formulated or have only partially formulated an investment plan. It explains ASIC's application of s1022 of the Corporations Law to ensure full disclosure of relevant matters, particularly the expertise of directors and management.
background: Under s1022 of the Corporations Law, prospectuses must contain all information investors reasonably require for an informed assessment. This guide is for issuers of such prospectuses, explaining ASIC's policy that the section does not prevent offers with undeveloped plans but requires high standards of disclosure about the skill and expertise of those making investment decisions.
ruling: ASIC believes s1022 is not intended to prevent offers but to ensure full disclosure. ASIC expects that where no investment plan exists, disclosure must focus on the expertise of directors and management, including qualifications, employment history, availability, and how their expertise will be deployed. If an investment plan is partially developed, all material details must be disclosed, including hypothetical portfolios and risk profiles. ASIC considers s1022(2)(b) imposes an active obligation on issuers to make reasonable enquiries about how proceeds would likely be invested.
